key_insight: CoFINN turns a CNN into a conservation-aware CFD surrogate by enforcing finite-volume flux consistency during training, rather than relying only on pixel-level errors.
engineering_relevance: This makes fast neural flow prediction more physically reliable for compressible aerodynamics, especially when shocks and limited data make standard CNN surrogates less trustworthy.
method: Treats the CNN output as a structured finite-volume grid
Computes conservation losses from numerical fluxes instead of only image similarity
Keeps the surrogate architecture-agnostic while aligning it with CFD-style physics
evidence_signal: On transonic airfoil cases at M=0.7 and Re=6×10^6, the method reduced drag prediction error by up to 34% at extreme angles of attack and by about 15% on average across the test set.
watch_item: Accuracy gains depend on correct flux discretization and stable training; care is needed when extending to new geometries or conservation settings.
paper_title: CoFINN: Conservation Flux Informed Neural Networks for Physics Problems Governed by Conservation Laws
